basic_info: 28-year-old male presenting with neck pain following a car accident one week ago
present_illness: Neck pain in the posterior region, rated 7/10, exacerbated by head movement, with associated headaches but no neurological symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness. The patient has tried ibuprofen for pain relief with some improvement. No prior imaging or specialist consultations have been conducted. The pain is localized to the neck and does not radiate. It is difficult to move the head around, and turning the neck from side to side or bending it back causes pain. The patient can still manage most daily activities. Mechanism of injury: The patient was wearing a seatbelt, and his head and neck were jerked forward really quickly when the car hit him from behind. He did not lose consciousness, but he did feel a lot of sudden pain right after it happened. The pain has stayed about the same, just getting worse when I move my neck. I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my arms or legs. I don't have any history of neck injuries or surgeries other than the car accident. I haven't had any balance issues, dizziness, or changes in vision since the accident.
